titleEn: Table Saw Partial Amputation - Tourniquet and TXA

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation

dispatchEn: 1005 hrs. Code 3 to a cabinet-making shop in an industrial park in Surrey. 52-year-old male caught his left forearm in a table saw. Coworkers report severe bleeding. Hospital is 12 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: coworkers are holding a towel on the arm and the machine has been shut off.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan tourniquet, pressure dressings, oxygen, amputated-part care, early transport
Anticipate machine hazard and blood exposure; PPE incl eye protection
Verbalize hazards (machine locked out, blood), environment, MOI (table saw), one patient; estimate blood loss
Don gloves and eye protection (splash risk)
First look: pale male, awake, large blood pool, near-complete amputation at the wrist
Attempt direct pressure; when it fails, apply a tourniquet proximal to the wound, tighten to stop the bleed, NOTE THE TIME, do not release
Assess circulation on the uninjured side; recognize shock
Complete the RBS for other injuries
Position supine, keep warm with blankets
Bandage the wound once hemorrhage is controlled
Categorize as RTC and act with urgency
Packaged and ready to load within 15 minutes
Delegate bystanders effectively (cot, doors, part preservation under direction)
HxC/C: mechanism, time of injury (critical for TXA window), blade contact points, LOC
BP by auscultation on the uninjured arm
BGL - indicated in a known diabetic
Upper extremities: tourniquet site, dressing, wound recheck
Wound management skill: tourniquet technique correct, time noted, bleeding controlled, wound bandaged
Preserve the amputated part correctly (moist sterile gauze, bag, kept cool, not on ice, transported with patient)
Execute the Hypovolemia protocol (supine, warm, O2, rapid transport)
PCP: IV, 20 mL/kg bolus reassessed q500 mL, and TXA 2 g IV over 1 min with 6 rights
Verbalize withholding Entonox due to shock caution
Reassess ABCs plus tourniquet/dressing after each move and each 500 mL
Second full vitals within 5-6 minutes; interpret the improving trend
Never release or loosen the tourniquet
Complete hand-off incl part preservation and drug times
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes (tourniquet and TXA times documented)

pcrFacts.cc: Near-complete left hand amputation proximal to wrist, arterial hemorrhage
pcrFacts.hxcc: Table saw caught glove while clearing jam ~0957; no LOC; pain 9/10; ~700 mL loss on scene
treatments: Direct pressure failed - tourniquet left forearm at 1012, never released
Part: saline-moist gauze, bagged, kept cool, transported with patient
PCP: IV, NS bolus q500 mL reassess, TXA 2 g IV at 1025
findings: Shock: BP 96/64, pulse 122, pale cool clammy

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR: tourniquet, part preservation, shock positioning, warmth, high-flow O2 and a 15-minute clock are all EMR-level skills - no IV, no TXA. Entonox withheld (shock caution).
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds vascular access on the intact arm, 20 mL/kg NS bolus (max 2 L, reassess q500 mL, target SBP 90) and TXA 2 g IV over 1 minute within the 3-hour window. Functional Enquiry en route.

_phaseScripts.dispatch: Dispatch update en route: coworkers are holding a towel on the arm and the machine has been shut off.
_phaseScripts.scene: EXAMINER SCRIPT: A coworker leads you in. The table saw is OFF and locked out. The patient sits on the floor leaning on a cabinet, a blood-soaked towel clamped to his left forearm. An estimated 700 mL of blood is pooled on the floor. The hand is attached only by a soft-tissue bridge just proximal to the wrist. One patient. Good lighting, no other hazards.
_phaseScripts.primary: ACTOR: alert, pale, frightened, gripping the towel. EXAMINER: when the towel is lifted, bright red blood SPURTS from the wound - direct pressure through dressings does NOT control it. This is hemorrhage requiring a tourniquet: apply proximal to the wound on the forearm, tighten until bleeding stops, NOTE THE TIME, never release. Airway clear; respirations 22; right radial pulse 122 weak. Skin (during RBS): pale, cool, clammy. RBS: no other injuries. SpO2 95% on O2. C-spine not indicated (no fall, no head involvement - machine injury only). UNSTABLE: tourniquet hemorrhage + shock signs.
_phaseScripts.transport: Decision point. Hemorrhage requiring a tourniquet + amputation proximal to the wrist + shock signs = UNSTABLE, RTC. Ready to load within 15 minutes. Delegate a coworker (under direction) to prepare the amputated-part container while you package.
_phaseScripts.history: EN ROUTE (or while partner packages). ACTOR: reached over the blade to clear a jam, glove caught, arm pulled in; happened about 8 minutes before arrival; no LOC, no other body part touched the blade. Pain 9/10. PMHx: type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol. Meds: metformin, atorvastatin. Allergies: sulfa drugs (hives). LOI: breakfast 0700, coffee since.
_phaseScripts.vitals: Set 1: GCS 15; BP 96/64; pulse 122 weak regular; respirations 22; skin pale cool clammy; pupils equal reactive; SpO2 95% on 15 L NRB; BGL 7.8 (indicated - known diabetic); temp not indicated. RTC interval 5-6 minutes.
_phaseScripts.fe: PCP ONLY, en route, brief for the unstable patient. ACTOR: general - felt lightheaded on scene; CNS nil; respiratory nil; cardiovascular - heart pounding; GI/GU - nauseated; integumentary - the wound; musculoskeletal nil elsewhere; endocrine - diabetes well controlled; EENT nil.
_phaseScripts.exam: EN ROUTE head-to-toe: head/neck nil; chest - clear, equal air entry 6 sites; abdomen soft; back nil; lower extremities nil; upper extremities - tourniquet in place, bleeding controlled, distal part cool and pulseless (expected distal to tourniquet), right arm normal.
_phaseScripts.interventions: Treatments: once the patient is stabilized, preserve the (near-)amputated part: rinse gross debris with cool sterile water, wrap loosely in saline-moistened sterile gauze, place in a plastic bag, keep the bag cool in a protective container, transport WITH the patient. Never warm it, never immerse in water, never place directly on ice, never use dry ice. Hypovolemia protocol: supine, warmth, O2. PCP EN ROUTE: vascular access on the right arm; fluid bolus 20 mL/kg max 2 L reassessing q500 mL (SBP target 90); TXA 2 g IV over 1 minute - indicated (shock from blood loss, well under 3 hours). Analgesia: Entonox is CAUTIONED in shock - withhold and document rationale.
_phaseScripts.ongoing: Reassess ABCs, the tourniquet and dressing after every move - the dressing must stay dry (no re-bleeding). Set 2 (en route, fluids running): GCS 15; BP 102/66; pulse 114; respirations 20; skin pale cool; pupils equal; SpO2 96% on 15 L; BGL not repeated. Improving with fluid.
_phaseScripts.handoff: Critical patient - en-route notification with tourniquet TIME clearly stated. Hand-off must mention the part, its packaging, and TXA time. PCR within 5 minutes.

_handoffModelEn: This is a 52-year-old male with a near-complete amputation of the left hand just proximal to the wrist from a table saw at approximately 0957, arterial bleeding uncontrolled by direct pressure. A tourniquet was applied to the left forearm at 1012 and has not been released. Estimated 700 mL blood loss on scene. Initial vitals GCS 15, BP 96/64, pulse 122 weak, resps 22, skin pale cool clammy, SpO2 95% on 15 litres, BGL 7.8; latest BP 102/66, pulse 114 after one litre of saline. History of type 2 diabetes and dyslipidemia on metformin and atorvastatin, allergic to sulfa. Treatments: tourniquet at 1012, pressure dressing, supine with warmth, high-flow oxygen, IV with saline bolus running, TXA 2 grams IV at 1025, and the amputated part is wrapped in saline-moistened gauze, bagged and kept cool, transported with him.
_criticalPitfallsEn: Finding life-threatening hemorrhage and failing to control it, or long delay before the tourniquet - 100% (RBS)
Releasing or loosening the tourniquet once applied - 100%
Not noting the tourniquet time - critical information failure carried into records deductions
Placing the part directly on ice, in water, or warming it - part-preservation errors (skill deductions)
PCP: skipping the reassessment every 500 mL during the bolus, or TXA outside its indications - protocol errors up to 100%
